AMZN.rationale: Amazon's franchise quality is among the strongest in global technology — dominant e-commerce (38.5% US share), AWS reaccelerating at 28% growth on a $150B base with $364B contracted backlog, advertising at $68.6B, and a pristine balance sheet (debt/equity 0.149, equity $369.6B). Q1 2026 showed record 13.1% operating margin and $181.5B revenue (+17% YoY), with Q2 guidance raised above consensus. However, the valuation is stretched: PE at 38.85x sits at the 12-month ceiling (range 28.2–39.0x), having expanded ~34% in three months while the stock rallied +31.8% quarterly. The earnings yield of 2.6% is deeply negative versus the 10-year Treasury at 4.45%. The Q1 2026 EPS beat of $2.78 is heavily inflated by a $16.8B non-cash mark-to-market gain on private AI investments; adjusted EPS is closer to $1.24, meaning the quality question persists in a different form than the quant report's Q3 2025 operating margin compression. The $200B 2026 capex cycle has collapsed trailing FCF to $1.2B (down 95%), introducing execution risk. Regulatory overhang (FTC trial October 2026) and rising long rates add further headwinds for a stock already priced for perfection. The business trajectory is genuinely strong, but the market has already priced it in aggressively — the risk-reward is unfavorable for new fundamental buyers at current levels.

sources_cited.excerpt: AWS is 18% of Amazon's revenue but produces 57% of its profit… Amazon generated $716.9 billion in total revenue… overall operating margin improved to 11.2% in 2025

Amazon holds an estimated 38.5 percent of the US e-commerce market… AWS accounted for roughly 13–15% of Amazon's consolidated revenue historically while delivering a disproportionately higher share of operating income

The FTC's broader antitrust case against Amazon, filed in 2023 and joined by 17 states, remains active… Tariff policy is the second pressure point… Amazon paid a record $2.5 billion to settle the FTC's Prime case in 2025, lost a €746 million GDPR appeal in the same year
